messages:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tune I see a tail-latency regression on prefill-heavy traffic (prefix/prompt cache hits). p95 up ~2.4x on the canary.
kevin: Which kernel change? the auto-select PR? @maria can you repro locally?
maria: Yes the auto-select that prefers the new 'fast-attn-fp16' kernel when seq_len<=128. Repro on canary: qps ~300, ~30% prefix-cache-hit. Profiling indicates tons of microbatches of size 1 during prefill->decode handoff.
dave: Microbatches of 1 for cached prefixes sounds like token-budget misalignment. If prefill is cached we end up issuing small decode-only requests and batcher thinks it should keep waiting for prefill tokens that never arrive.
angela: Also saw that fast-attn-fp16 doesn't support zero-copy kv access on this driver, so we fall back to a copy path that adds ~6ms per request.
cache-bot: cache-metrics: cache-hit-rate=0.32; avg_prefill_tokens=22; avg_gen_tokens=8; prefills_with_kv=0.29
maria: Dumped a short trace and kernel timeline (excerpt):

```
[sched] req=0x7f... prefill_hit=true -> batcher.enqueue(decode-only)
[kernel] select=fast-attn-fp16 (no-kv-fastpath)
[copy] kv-copy start
[kernel] exec decode
```

That kv-copy happens for every single-request decode and kills throughput.
kevin: Can you paste the batcher config used in canary?
maria: Current canary config:

```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 32
  prefill_budget: 64
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
  wait_ms: 6
  enable_prefill_coalesce: false
```

dave: Two quick ideas: 1) make the batcher kv-cache-aware so decode-only enqueues can be packed with pending prefill-affine requests (coalesce_prefill=true). 2) increase token_budget_target and prefill_budget to avoid immediate flush of 1-token microbatches.
angela: Also consider forcing kernel selection to prefer 'kv-friendly' kernels when request.prefill_hit==true. That avoids the copy path.
kevin: Agreed. Small config experiment first before kernel policy change.
maria: Did a 30m micro-canary with these tweaks:

```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 128
  prefill_budget: 256
  enable_prefill_coalesce: true
  kv_aware_packing: true
```

Result: p95 from 380ms -> 210ms on prefill-heavy traces. microbatch size median 1->6. Cost +2% (GPU util up), tail much tighter.
dave: Nice. Any regressions on gen-heavy workloads?
maria: Ran a 1h smoke on mixed traffic — gen-heavy p50/p95 stable, slight p50 up ~5ms.
kevin: Please open a PR with config keys and add unit tests for coalesce logic. Also we need a fallback: if kernel lacks kv-fastpath then treat prefill_hit as not beneficial for that kernel.
maria: PR opened: #4821 (config + unit tests + perf run logs). Deployed to canary cluster pg-3.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/pg-3 by maria at 2026-03-18T15:42:00Z :rocket:
angela: We should also add a regression alert tied to prompt set "prefill-heavy" (eval harness) — if p95 increases >20% raise page.
kevin: I'll add an alert and schedule a 6h rush-hour canary tonight.
dave: One more operational note: add a per-model knob to disable fast-attn-fp16 auto-select when model has heavy prefix-cache usage historically.
maria: Agreed. I'll update PR with model selector flag + run longer perf tomorrow.
kevin: Thanks all. Good outcome — we have a fast mitigation path (batcher tuning) and medium-term fix (kernel selection policy).
